label: churn200-s4
summary: The model predicts churn as the logistic function of six leaf parts added on the log-odds scale (training AUC 0.911; mean prediction 14.0% against an observed rate of 14.1%). The strongest group reads daytime usage and customer service calls; replacing it by its baseline drops training AUC to 0.696. Service calls work as a hinge: for a typical customer predicted churn is 1.6% with a single call, 9.9% with four and 27.4% with five, because a gate cancels the direct calls term until the calls are high. Daytime usage is flat and then steep: with matching day charge, 1.5% at two hundred minutes, 11.2% at two hundred and fifty and 91.3% at three hundred; heavy evening use lowers, and a voicemail plan raises, the daytime level at which the usage gate opens. Many calls and heavy use stack: 92.0% with five calls and two hundred and eighty day minutes. An international plan takes the typical customer from 1.6% to 17.1%; a voicemail plan lowers predicted churn, more international calls lower it and a low daytime charge, together with a low international charge, raises it. State offsets follow each state's observed churn rate (Hawaii -1.95 on the log-odds, Washington 1.19), each fitted to one state's customers (Hawaii 73, Washington 72). Coverage is full and the annotated model reproduces the network to 4.4e-16.

tool_bugs: update_narrative: allow_numbers must be a JSON list string; a comma-separated string makes xn.py crash with a JSONDecodeError traceback instead of returning an error. xn.py --render has no allow-list option, so literal probe settings in narratives always appear as lint errors there although update_narrative accepts them with allow_numbers. get_formula returns no provenance id, so formula evidence is attached as a typed LaTeX payload. Evidence records cannot be deleted: one accidental duplicate closed-form record on usage_gate (a repeated batch call) was marked as a duplicate with amend_evidence.
